speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg started and how long it has been there? Please also tell me if you have any history of diabetes, vascular disease, or recent injuries to that area.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion following an insect bite, I suspect an inflammatory condition like pyoderma gangrenosum rather than a simple infection. Does the border of the ulcer have a distinct purple or blue hue, and have you noticed any new joint pain or worsening of your bowel symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of dilated, tortuous veins and pitting edema strongly suggests underlying venous insufficiency, which is a common cause of leg ulcers. To distinguish this from pyoderma gangrenosum or other causes, I need to assess the local circulation. REQUEST TEST: Ankle_Branch_Index

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal Ankle-Brachial Index rules out significant arterial disease, and the history of Crohn's disease combined with the ulcer's purplish borders and pathergy (onset after an ant bite) strongly points to Pyoderma Gangrenosum. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out underlying infection or vasculitis, I need to see the lesion and check for systemic inflammation. REQUEST IMAGES
REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive_Protein
REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: C-Reactive_Protein: Elevated; Wound_Culture: No growth

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated CRP indicates significant systemic inflammation, while the negative wound culture rules out a primary infectious cause, which aligns perfectly with an autoimmune etiology. Given the history of Crohn's disease, the pathergy triggered by the ant bite, and the characteristic purplish borders, the clinical picture is consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
